qualification: Exact selected engine/caller and content paths; not whole-game semantic, runtime or balance acceptance. Original proposals are separately ranked in PACKETS.json.

findings.title: Discovery is separate from use
findings.finding: Spell discovery visibility joins visibility prerequisites, recipe-book availability and prerequisite spells. CanDiscover checks visibility and prerequisite spells. Discover marks the recipe discovered and calls PostDiscoverRecipe, which optionally adds an unaugmented instance to the current loadout when a slot and usage capacity are available.
limits: Selected named prerequisite/book bindings are reviewed in claims022–029; broader recipes and live scene callback paths remain outside this sample. Duplicate PostDiscoverRecipe call remains a qualified source-route caveat.

findings.title: Use prerequisites impose penalties
findings.finding: A spell lacking usagePrerequisites can still be cast if charges, attunement and resources allow it. Its upfront cost receives insufficientReqCostMod; its loaded cooldown receives insufficientReqCdMod; its loadout usage adds penaltyUsageCost before reductions and clamps to zero. Augmented creation UI disables augments on a recipe whose usage prerequisites are unmet.
limits: Installed numeric penalties are closed by OOC-SPELL-021; current player modifiers/UI remain unverified.

findings.title: Casting gates and queue
findings.finding: Player mouse-down/hotkey routes call Fire. Fire attempts Cast only if CanCast; otherwise an active spell can cancel if the setting permits. Cast refuses duplicate readiness, queues behind any preparing/charging/waiting-input spell, interrupts active channels, snapshots cast data/effects/cooldown, spends upfront cost unless flash, then starts preparation. Queue capacity is one, and the queued attempt is removed whether it succeeds or fails when readiness clears.
limits: No guarantee of an explicit error popup for unaffordable manual attempts; Fire normally leaves state unchanged.

findings.title: Actual expenditure and capacity are distinct
findings.finding: HasEnough checks each ResourceSO.HasAmount. Normal costs compare stock against amount divided by resource quality; bandwidth costs check missing usage capacity. PerformCost calls Spend, whose normal branch changes stock, rest/loss state and optional decay/replenish accumulations. PerformUsage records usage instead of consuming stock; loadout usage recomputation removes and reapplies a single calculator GUID.

findings.title: Preparation and charging timing
findings.finding: Preparation time is recipe.castSpeed / (castSpeedMod * playerCastSpeedPercent) expressed as percentage division. Increment counts preparation down at the current cast-speed percentage and carries the leftover frame into execution. When charge power exceeds101 and an input remains held, charging uses max charge time plus0.67 padding, counts down at cast speed, then interpolates power and special effect by the held fraction; release executes early. WaitingInput holds readiness until result targeting is ready.
limits: Exact recipe times/player charge stats are serialized. This is source timing, with no launched-game or frame-order observation.

findings.title: Execution has multiple real consumers
findings.finding: ExecuteSpell builds an animation payload for instant effects, sets up persistent channel/aura effects and glyph on-cast effects, increments total casts and updates its own spell-cast recharge tracker. Manual instant spells return idle and consume a charge; manual casts award player casting XP and recipe mastery XP and schedule any echo records. Instant resource scripts can gain adjusted stock, a percentage of current capacity, or an amount based on current true rate; gains obey resource capacity/overflow rules.
limits: Animation payload execution can delay visible mutation; named effects/resources are bound in later claims, while other recipes remain unread.

findings.title: Channel and aura upkeep and stop
findings.finding: Channel/Aura are toggled spells. They add persistent status effects with drain based on active scaling and a duration determined by maxChannel. They can gain casting XP rate and recipe mastery over held time. Starting another cast interrupts Channels. Timed duration, status expiry, or enabled manual cancellation ends casting, removes XP rate/effects/drain, and consumes a manual charge, activating loaded recovery. Resource status expires when its effective drain ratio is below1 and a drained resource is at zero.
limits: Auras are not interrupted by StopCastingChannelled. A manual toggled spell does not recharge through the Casting branch until it ends; externally cast toggled spells do.

findings.title: Charge recovery modules and sequential recovery
findings.finding: Cooldown is loaded before preparation, then charge is consumed after instant execution or toggled end. Base cooldown is floored at a quarter of recipe.baseRecharge.duration, then modified by player/type/glyph/per-level factors and soft prerequisite penalty. Recovery sums modules for elapsed Unity time, total spells cast and attributes developed; glyph modules multiply by stack count. Idle recovery decrements loaded cooldown at current recovery-speed percentage; restoring a charge can activate the next loaded cooldown and carry overshoot, with a0.01 minimum.
limits: Source units differ by module. A Number-of-Casts recovery label is not wall-clock seconds. Own ExecuteSpell updates its cast tracker after incrementing total casts, excluding that own execution from its recovery delta.

findings.title: Loadout changes preserve spent state
findings.finding: Swap is rejected during Casting or ReadyingCast. Valid swap stores a shallow copy of active Spell objects, clears outgoing echo records, stops outgoing attunement, installs saved objects, optionally restores equipment/alchemy, starts one second of attunement for incoming spells, and recalculates usage. Depleted charges alone do not reject a swap. Inactive loadouts call spell.Increment only when inactiveCooldownSpeed>0, scaled by that percentage.
limits: Authored inactive recovery is1.2% before modifiers, closed by OOC-SPELL-021.

findings.title: Removing a spell is constrained by recovery
findings.finding: Removal refuses spells that lack maximum charges or are casting/readying. If such a spell lacks a Time recharge module, the rejected removal adds a temporary0.5 time module and temporarily disables existing modules, allowing recovery to finish. Full recharge removes temporary modules and reenables the originals. Successful removal deletes the instance and recalculates usage.

findings.title: Glyph combinations alter function and payment
findings.finding: Augment glyphs adjust power, special effect, duration, upfront/drain cost, cooldown/base cooldown, cast speed, XP, critical/echo parameters, charges and recovery modules. Base resource cost adds each distinct glyph extra cost then combines conversion tables: IncludeConvertList splits matched cost among target types and retains an original share when the original is not already among targets, using rarity ratios for conversions. Drain cost also uses conversion tables. Elemental glyph types precede original elemental types, limited to three total spell types after preserving non-elemental types.
limits: Per-stack modifier effects use quantity; the base-added resource cost iterates distinct glyphs. Do not presume every modifier field is assigned in an installed glyph.

findings.title: Glyph availability and preparation rules
findings.finding: Non-discoverable glyph availability checks prerequisites; discoverable ones require discovered. Selection caps added stacks at glyph.GetMaxUsages. Glyph duration/toggle requirements restrict creation, and loadout-unique types reject duplicate recipes in creation UI. A mastery requirement number is computed and displayed but is absent from the reviewed recipe-button disabled expression; do not report it as an enforced mastery gate in this build.
limits: Creation UI routes and controls still need installed scene binding.

findings.title: Glyph leveling and loadout free-use budget
findings.finding: Each six total glyph levels yields another free per-spell usage; levels also raise maximum stacks and apply authored leveling effects. Glyph usage prerequisites multiply usage cost by the global glyph usage penalty. Loadout calculator uses per-spell free uses first, then spends a shared freeLoadoutUses budget sequentially in loadout order. Reordering can shift which spell bears a usage cost without changing the total eligible stack budget.
limits: Glyph GetUsageCostOfRecord has a separate branch for nonpositive base rarity costs. Record exact behavior rather than assuming a universal subtract-free-stacks formula.

findings.title: Mastery feeds type progression
findings.finding: Manual execute XP derives from normalized base-cost rarity plus half base cooldown and multiplies level, glyph/type/player/recipe XP factors. Held XP derives from base drain rarity with a channel multiplier. Gaining XP readies mastery, but confirming mastery requires a separate purchase action and resource cost. PurchaseLevel increments mastery and grants type XP to each original spell type, then applies authored per-mastery power/cost/recovery/duration/special modifiers; type levels apply further stats and persistent effects.
limits: Mastery XP and confirmation-cost curves are serialized. Direct PurchaseLevel lacks a payment itself; the reviewed UI cost button/bulk route owns payment.

findings.title: Echo, critical and flash are distinct
findings.finding: Manual cast samples critical and echo levels from RatingReport and flash from a diminishing-return chance. Critical multiplies power/duration. Echo is unavailable to Channels; execution schedules echo instances with delay i*recipe.castSpeed, power attenuation by chain index, and zero drain-cost modifier. Delayed records decrement with cast speed only while Idle. Echo/External execution does not follow manual expenditure, charge-consumption or execute-XP branch. Flash manual cast skips upfront payment and divides preparation and loaded cooldown by flash effect, but CanCast still required affordable resources before the flash roll.
limits: Spell.cs1697–1735 repeatedly uses critical type fields in flash/echo aggregators; avoid assuming designer intent or correcting source. Exact player/type/glyph stats await assets.

findings.title: Data-driven external-cast mechanism
findings.finding: InstantSpellEffect selects nonempty spells matching SpellCondition and SampleListTarget. CooldownAdjust changes active cooldown. InstantCast adds an External cast with staggered delay, externally specified level and power multiplied by the target spell power. External instances execute from Idle; this supports data-driven combinations and automatic effects, with installed Reverberate binding (023); AutomagicTome is instead passive amplification (029). SpellCondition can filter type, recipe, critical and echo states; SampleListTarget either takes all or samples a size, repeating selection the authored number of times. No affordability, charge or cooldown filter appears in the external-cast selector itself.
limits: No automagic or scroll mechanic symbol was found in managed source searches. That is a source-access limit, not proof the game lacks those features.
Generic source trace is qualified by installed claims OOC-SPELL-023 through030.

findings.title: Glyph global tokens can fund later passive reactions
findings.finding: Glyph on-cast effects generate scaled global passive tokens; while casting they add token rate, with different source bases for aura and channel. PassiveAbility checks reaction cooldown, chance, affordability, token availability and trigger validity, then spends real resources/tokens and executes authored entry effects. Passive repeats execute authored blocks on their TickTimer, stop when effects are removed, and token rates/durations can change retained tokens.
limits: Generic source trace is qualified by installed claims OOC-SPELL-023 through030.
Bound affinity/Hasted passives have no repeat timer or reaction listeners; generic reaction costs do not describe those three.

findings.title: Creation cost and legacy methods need route qualification
findings.finding: GetSpellCreateCost starts with an empty resource-cost list and applies augment cost modifiers, so no base creation debit is established by that formula. Discovered CreateRecipe adds a prepared augmented spell and attunes it without an explicit PerformCost. UI methods and informational per-spell level setters coexist with global output-level getters; SetSelectedLevel is empty and Spell.SetLevel recomputes cost only. Exact active scene/prefab bindings are required before treating every legacy UI path as current gameplay.
limits: This is an uncertainty note, not a tested game defect. Serialized Unity callbacks and UICostButton.performCost can select different actual routes.

findings.title: Prerequisite success is cached
findings.finding: Prerequisites.Container.Check rechecks individual conditions only until all pass, then latches available=true. CheckChange rechecks only while unavailable. Reset clears that latch. Spell and glyph usage-prerequisite checks therefore do not guarantee continuous revalidation of an underlying condition after success; exact condition kind determines what achievement is being latched.
limits: Do not describe this generic container as a continuously maintained fuel requirement; cast costs and status drain are independent current-stock consumers.

findings.title: Consumable preparation is a separate spell-combination route
findings.finding: Generic consumables require current count, cost affordability, usage capacity and no cooldown. SelectAndFire pre-pays each queued use cost. Inventory queues distinct consumable types and prepares the front type. PrepNextUsage selects the strongest count, creates/hydrates effects, loads cooldown, reserves duration usage and removes that inventory count before preparation finishes. Preparation runs at consumable prep speed and waits for targeting; completed use executes instant effects and duration status, then advances the queue. Cancellation removes queued usage without an explicit count/cost refund in this method.
limits: Replenish item procs can refund cost and produce a free consumable after successful use (ConsumableSO379–388), so consumption is conditional on current ratings.
Generic source trace is qualified by installed claims OOC-SPELL-023 through030.

findings.title: Installed numerical penalties and percentage units
findings.finding: Installed GlobalValues insufficientReqCdMod and insufficientReqCostMod both serialize adjust 1 as MultiStacking, yielding multiplier 2 after deserialization. Glyph usage penalty is also multiplier 2. InactiveCooldownSpeed authored base 1.2 contributes 1.2%, or factor 0.012, before current modifiers: its getter reaches BigDouble.AsPercent, which shifts exponent by minus two.
limits: Installed authored bases are not current player stats. Matching firstpass method evidence is pinned separately.

findings.title: Named production has coupled inputs
findings.finding: GatherKnowledge has authored discovery/cast entries of 100 Mana, a 1 Knowledge gain effect, 1s windup and 10s time recovery. Construct has 40 VerdantEnergy discovery, 130 Mana plus 8 Knowledge cast input, a 0.02 Skill gain effect, 1s windup and 12s recovery. Both are Cantrips. Their gains reach actual ResourceSO quantity, quality/gain/capacity and mastery consumers through SpellEffect scaling.
limits: Amounts are base entries before output level, player/type/glyph effects and quality; not promised effective casts.

findings.title: Reverberate is one finite external dispatch
findings.finding: Reverberate has 35 Spark base cost, 0.67s windup, 40s time recovery and 6 WeightSpell occupancy; soft use readiness is ExpertWizardry >=11 and ExpertStorm >=5. It selects every nonempty active Cantrip once in loadout order and schedules External records at 0.33*(index+1) delay. Its target-level conversion follows casting level; base external power is 80 before special scaling and target power. External records wait for that target to be Idle, tick delay at target cast speed, bypass target affordability/charges/upfront spend/manual XP/charge consumption, still increment total casts and trigger glyph/passive effects, and can roll critical/flash. They never create another manual Echo chain. This binding has no repeated timer.
limits: Authored active-slot base is 3 before modifiers; selector has no additional record cap. Reverberate is not a Cantrip and does not redispatch itself.

findings.title: External channels keep upkeep and delayed work
findings.finding: ChannelSpark is a Cantrip Channel with 130 Mana startup entry, 40 Mana/s drain, 16s duration, 45s recovery and 1 WeightSpell; it adds 1.1 Spark rate and conditionally buffs Cantrip recovery speed after ChannelSparkSpeed purchase. ChannelBlaze is also Cantrip Channel, with 600 Mana startup, 250 Mana/s drain and 12s duration. Reverberate bypasses startup and manual charge loss but retains drain scaling. External execution skips the manual channel-interruption call, admitting concurrent channels; resource depletion still expires them. Swap removes only Echo records, so delayed External records survive outgoing swap. Inactive increments require positive inactive speed; delayed-record countdown does not use the inactive recovery multiplier.
limits: Concurrent external channels and inactive delayed records are source-admitted, unplayed exceptional branches.

findings.title: Work buffs have different duration and swap rules
findings.finding: ManaForge is an Aura with 300 Mana base cast input, 15s duration, 40s recovery and 5 WeightSpell. ExpertWizardry >=8 and ExpertArtificer >=3 are soft readiness; AspectWorkshop controls visibility. It increases BuildingResourceType GainRate (+0.2 diminishing), WorkshopStructures BuildSpeed (+0.8 diminishing) and PowerBuildRating (+4 raw) under scaling. StructureType records propagate to real structures and the action scheduler consumes buffed build speed. Meditation Aura pays 200 Mana and 2 PsychicEnergy/s for 22s, boosts elemental gains and MentalAffinity token rate, and needs ExpertScholar >=3 softly. Haste is Instant with a separate stacking 18s status affecting SwiftStructures power and Hasted token rate. It returns Idle, so the status can persist across loadout swap; active ManaForge/Meditation blocks swap.
limits: Costs, durations and coefficients are authored before current scaling, not final elapsed runtime.

findings.title: Named glyph tradeoffs change ordinary preparation
findings.finding: Quick adds one WeightSpell, raises upfront cost by stacking 15% and reduces cooldown by stacking 30%; it does not directly change cast speed. Efficient needs ExpertAugments >=3 softly, adds one WeightSpell, divides power by 1.1 for an unmodified single stack and uses stacking -0.3 on both upfront cost and drain; it creates ElementalAffinity tokens. Resourceful needs ExpertAugments >=12 softly, adds one WeightSpell, raises power by stacking 8%, cost by stacking 20% and cast speed by diminishing 10%, and adds AttributesDeveloped recovery module multiplier 1 per stack. Real developed attributes can repay recovery. Repeating needs ExpertAugments >=16 softly; its leveling-effects binding raises global SpellEchoRating rather than its per-spell spellDoubleCastRating field. It is not perpetual autocasting.
limits: Single-stack coefficients precede type-specific glyph bonuses, modifiers and augment resonance; discovery has separate books/prerequisites.

findings.title: Scrolls prepare retained work capacity
findings.finding: ScrollPower/ScrollSpeed have zero base cooldown, 1s prep, 2 PotionToxicity use cost and no temporary usage reservation. They select a visible Structure in AllStructures that can receive a stronger relevant enchantment, then retain EnchantPower/EnchantSpeed. Power enchant applies diminishing 0.03 Power at order -1 under EnchantmentScaling. Speed enchant applies diminishing 0.2 BuildSpeed under EnchantmentScalingMicro and raw +2 EffectLevel under EnchantmentScaling. The same-kind old enchantment is removed before replacement; a stronger old instance rejects weaker replacement. Structure initialization reapplies retained enchantments. Random selection picks greatest enchantment separation; manual input can wait or cancel. No valid target cancels usage after the generic route paid use cost and consumed a selected count, with no refund in that branch.
limits: Cancellation consequence is source behavior, not a launched UI defect; UI may block that route. ScrollEcho targeting/cost was read, but its Echo-build enchant consumer was not closed.

findings.title: Scroll acquisition is a paid work stage
findings.finding: CraftScrollPower needs purchased ScribeScroll2. Authored recipe entries are 7e18 Magebloom, 2e22 ThaumicScroll and 1e8 Ink, with base duration 720s, useQuantityAsLevel=true and ScrollCostScaling. Completion creates ScrollPower scaled through EnchantmentScaling. UI queue checks recipe affordability and capacity, pays GetTotalCost through PurchaseQuantity, then creates or extends a manual CraftingInstance; completion occurs once. Quantity, magnitude and speed change the actual duration and resource expenditure.
limits: Base entries are not final current prices/waits. Full scribing automation is separately owned.

findings.title: Automagic is passive amplification with stops
findings.finding: AutomagicTome is a Workshop structure, available after ConstructionBook2 purchase with ExpertAugments >=2 soft readiness. It has authored base inputs 90 Thaumaturgy and 2 ThaumicScroll, no own drainCost, and a diminishing 0.16 Power contribution to AuraStructures scaled by its real structure power/quantity. Type registration propagates that contribution into owned aura properties. Contribution stops when quantity is zero, the Tome is disabled or its effective drain ratio is zero; the Tome itself has no fuel-drain stop. AutomagicControl and Cognitive Automagic further modify retained Tome Power. This is passive amplification, not automatic Fire/queued-spell selection. Affected aura outputs and their own fuel/capacity remain resource-lane consumers.
limits: All spell/glyph/passive/consumable reference-type entries were scanned for Spell/InstantSpellEffect; only Reverberate matched. This bounded entry-point scan is not full semantic coverage of every automatic system.

findings.title: Automatic benefits are capped and fade
findings.finding: Efficient casts/held glyphs supply ElementalAffinity tokens; Meditation supplies MentalAffinity token rate; Haste supplies Hasted token rate. These authored global passives have no repeating timer or reaction listeners. Affinity benefits require at least 1 token, cap effective whole tokens at base 10 and have base token duration 3.2s; Hasted has base cap 10 and duration 1.8s. Token ratios change actual resource quality/gain/rate or speed-group modifiers. Global tokenRate applies each frame. After the paid spell/status stops supplying rate, timed token loss eventually withdraws benefits. Internal accumulation may retain one fractional token above the cap, but GetWholeTokens caps effective benefit.
limits: Token duration/cap modifiers can change these bases; no optimized cast rotation or attainable ten-token claim.

findings.title: Effective input units
findings.finding: Costs divide nominal units by quality; effective quantity multiplies by quality. Generation applies gainRate; refunds divide by quality and bypass extra gainRate. Quality can change affordability without changing raw quantity.

findings.title: Passive cap versus active overflow
findings.finding: Passive incremental net gains call GainInternal without overflow; active rate permits overflow, and above cap passive positive delta is suppressed. Direct Gain requests overflow, subject to canOverflow and player modifiers. Overflow uses geometric diminishing gain with1000-sequence bound; excess has85%-scaled loss plus ordinary loss/baseLoss after loss mode engages. Active changes can reset the3-second loss timer. Authored flags must be resolved per resource. Here active/passive means ModifierRecord category, not whether the human clicked. ResourceGenerator adds its generated rates with the default Passive category, so both manual and automated resource rates normally meet passive caps; direct final remainder or instant Gain takes the direct-gain overflow path.

findings.title: Material bottleneck throttles actual work
findings.finding: ResourceDrain notifies consumers with the smallest supported input ratio. Near depleted stock, no base/splash production returns zero support; otherwise support depends on available production/stock. The least-supported input retains its drain quote while other inputs scale by the bottleneck ratio. Consumers multiply production/time by GetRatio, so empty inputs slow or stall real work.

findings.title: Bandwidth reserves shared capacity
findings.finding: Bandwidth quantity is usage, not spendable stock. HasAmount checks missing usage capacity; GUID reservations are added/removed. Functional capacity can propagate provider drain support through usageDrainPenalty. Missing functional capacity yields zero usage support; over-allocation uses0.25 raised to effective penalty count. One starved capacity provider can affect its reserved consumers.

findings.title: Manual crafting selects bulk and queue topology
findings.finding: Recipe prerequisites control visibility. UI chooses stacking or separate jobs, gates space/affordability, and pays modified total material cost before creating a job. Bulk grows completion time and can reduce output efficiency; quantity-as-level recipes use one output at chosen level. All manual and automatic entries count toward the source-supported shared multi-craft speed calculation; actual zero/nonzero type tuning is claim022.

findings.title: Automation drains inputs repeatedly
findings.finding: Automation adjusts one instance per recipe, represents non-level magnitude with powers of2 and reserves list space. Its maximum derives from input capacity times1000. Ongoing drain scales with quantity/cost/speed/time; output scales with output/time. Automation and authored parallel penalties can modify speed; claim022 qualifies the current material type. Completion repeats instead of expiring. CraftingManager parallelPower is not used by the reviewed live path.

findings.title: Cancel and completion have different consequences
findings.finding: CancelCraft removes rates/effects/drains without a manual-cost refund there. Output resources are generated during the job, with the remaining balance delivered near one-shot completion. Completion-only effects require completion. Thus already-produced stock, paid inputs and unfinished completion reward remain distinct.

findings.title: Alchemy slots differ from process copies
findings.finding: List capacity has typed and typeless recipe slots. Existing recipes accept more copies without another entry. UI checks space, free usage, bandwidth and mastery limits. Copy increases wait0.25 seconds; decreases apply immediately. Queued copies reserve bandwidth immediately. Free copies avoid bandwidth charge but active material drains remain.

findings.title: Alchemy has engaged and retained consequences
findings.finding: Engagement applies drains, usage, persistent effects and optional equip blocks. Persistent effects scale with input support; equip blocks force drain ratio1. Completion accumulates recipe-owned time scaled by support, necessary output demand and speed; executes instant effects, earns mastery and optional advancement. Disengaging removes active costs/effects, while recipeTime is not cleared in that path.

findings.title: Learning and overdrive retain tradeoffs
findings.finding: Unmet usage prerequisites can increase usage/drain and reduce speed or advancement scaling; effect conversion exponent is0.97. Copies beyond free allotment use diminishing overdrive power/speed and reduction-form drain adjustment. Recipe mastery contributes to linked types, whose modifiers propagate to all registered recipes. Paid level upgrades require mastery and authored prerequisites.

findings.title: Artifacts require creation and current allocation
findings.finding: UI labels EquipmentSO as Restore Artifact. Shared discoverable UI matches glyph/resource tuples and a cost button charges before Discover sets creation. Type created count can increase creation cost. Equip is limited by list/type space, allowed stacks and effective usage; unmet usage prerequisites double reservation. New/increased allocation waits for attunement, applies scaled persistent effects, earns mastery and updates total equipment mastery. Unequip frees usage/effects. Direct Create itself does not enforce payment.

findings.title: Artifact production combinations need real targets
findings.finding: Artifact equip blocks use current level/power and real PersistentEffectBlock execution. Resource effects write chosen resource channels; type registries attach channels to resources, alchemy recipes and crafting recipes. This routing supports changing gain, quality, capacity or recipe production, but a named artifact combination requires its serialized target/effect binding.

findings.title: Enchantments target structures in this assembly
findings.finding: StructureSO implements IEnchantable and initializes saved table effects; EquipmentSO does not. EnchantItemScript resolves an actual IEnchantable target. Same-type enchantments replace old effects unless the old level is higher; stronger comparison uses level only. Different types coexist. TargetStructure checks visibility/conditions and upgrade eligibility; automatic selection favors greatest level-times-power separation.

findings.title: Facility loops use ordered combinations
findings.finding: Facility ingredient slots use Resource/Glyph/Consumable types. Valid ordered tuples load a recipe inactive; invalid tuples clear it. Activation drains input over recipe time and loops at speed times actual support. Level selection clamps, deactivates and recomputes cost/time. Completion executes gain effects; active effects scale with difficulty/time/support. Each facility instance keeps its own recipe.

findings.title: Harvesting balances regeneration and extraction
findings.finding: HarvestElement creates an internal growing stock/capacity, then harvesting drains it plus authored inputs. Instances reserve usage and toggle production; output/mastery reduce with support. Extra harvest actions consume inputs and optional element stock, scale by support, and max at mastery+1. Passive generation needs visibility and autoGenerationMod greater than100.

findings.title: Research consumes capacity and accumulated materials
findings.finding: Development reserves escalating research usage and drains material totalCost into separate fill entries. Completion requires all entries; filled entries stop draining. Pause keeps investment, cancel clears investment/queue without refund there. Completed stages/levels reset fill, apply research effects and enable prerequisite links. Queued levels check cumulative development capacity/range and continue after completion.

findings.title: Structures preserve operating input constraints
findings.finding: Structures pay next cost before queueing construction and completed quantity changes level. Operating drain scales by quantity. Effects disappear at zero support, zero quantity or disabled; otherwise scale by support and quantity power. Enchantment targets the same structure. DisableStructure removes effects but does not remove the drain in that method, so input release is not promised.

findings.title: Alchemy inventory output has preparation and failure costs
findings.finding: ConsumableGainEffect grants filtered scaling. Full carry load can stop necessary alchemy drain; direct gain can reject lower-level arrivals or discard weakest copies. Inventory queues sequential preparation. Selection pays consumeCost; preparation removes strongest stored copy, starts cooldown and reserves duration usage. Ready/hydrated effects execute after prep; duration effects expire/release usage. Cancellation has no automatic refund in this path. Replenish rating may refund cost/grant free copies after successful nonfree use. Gain script calls once irrespective of external completion ratio, so batch output count must not be inferred from num alone.

findings.title: Legacy method names are not discovery proof
findings.finding: AlchemyManager.GetAlchemyFromCombo returns null and SelectAlchemyRecipe is empty. AlchemyRecipeSO glyph/resource recipe getters return empty lists. Shared discoverable UI handles exact artifact glyph matches and recipe-book discovery exists separately. Actual alchemy discovery needs scene/book binding rather than a legacy method-name claim.

findings.title: Wood supply is a coupled material/capacity loop
findings.finding: Extract Wood uses2200Wood/s and1Mechanical Capacity to supply4functional Biotic Capacity. Transmute Wood needs3Alchemical+1Biotic,0.12Control/s, and at default scaling supplies4000Wood rate plus a stacking x1.3Wood GainRate engagement effect. Its soft usage requirements are ExpertAlchemy2 and ExpertDruid2. It consumes no Wood itself; Extract Wood does. Functional Biotic capacity depends on supplied extraction; input starvation propagates via usageDrainPenalty to transmutation. Output and quoted input scale with levels/copies/modifiers. Transmute Wood also increases gains from other Wood sources while engaged because the equip block targets Wood GainRate, not a private output counter.

findings.title: Wooden Supports fund real production/capacity improvements
findings.finding: Wooden Supports craft consumes2000Skill+4000Wood+100ForceBark with30-second base time and outputs1WoodenSupport. Twelve structure baseCost consumers were found by field-only scanning. Notes specifically spends5Supports+50Paper and improves power of Scholar's Book and Magic Book. Scholar's Book changes Mental/Energy resource capacity, including Knowledge; Magic Book scales Magic resource rates, including existing Mana production. Woodbeams uses100Supports+100Wood to boost Wood Axe and Charger. Thus supports are actually spent in a later improvement with resource consumers rather than a decorative intermediate material.

findings.title: Current craft tuning differs from generic defaults
findings.finding: Material Crafting type has magnitudeLoss42, magnitudeTime2, automation speed stacking factor0.1, and multi-craft Reduction modifier0. The reviewed algorithm counts all concurrent jobs, but this specific type currently adds no multi-craft slowdown. Therefore do not present default50% multi penalty or generic parallel competition as the actual Wooden Supports tuning. Bulk output/time and90% automation slowdown remain actual tradeoffs before earned modifiers.

findings.title: Brewing Rod changes actual material work through a potion
findings.finding: Brewing Rod costs15000ForceBark+4000Water to create, reserves5Artifact Capacity per stack, and wants ExpertArtificer6 plus ExpertItems12 for effective use. Its equip blocks alter Brewing Power/Speed/ExperienceRate with baseline stacking factors1.12/1.6/1.3 before equipment scaling. Brew Woodwork Potion is a real Brewing+Alchemy recipe with350-second base completion,1Mechanical+4Biotic usage and authored Elementia drain. Completion creates Woodwork Potion; use costs8Toxicity, takes3seconds prep and has11-second base duration. Active effects alter Building Quality(+7%) and Parchment Quality(+5%) plus stacking GainRate factors1.4, subject to potion scaling. Wood and Wooden Supports are Building resources, so quality changes actual input amounts and gain changes actual output. Faster brewing also increases material drain per second through GetBaseDrainCostMod. Base Mechanical Capacity1 cannot simultaneously support Extract Wood and this brew without added capacity or another supply choice.

findings.title: Catalyst is an alternative scarce tool, not a free stacked buff
findings.finding: Philosopher's Catalyst uses550Control+500OccultEssence creation inputs and5Artifact+1Runic capacity per stack. Effective-use requirements are ExpertArtificer13 and ExpertAlchemy16. It adds10%Alchemical Capacity, applies globalAlchemy DrainCost stacking factor0.4 and an AlchemyPowerGroup stacking factor1.2 before equipment scaling. That group binds Transmutation Power at full ratio, Refinement Power at0.7 ratio and Essence rate at0.7/order-1. findings.claim: Required visible discoveries supersede random offers. Other offers are undiscovered+visible items; the algorithm guarantees ready candidates when available and can include future-use candidates, weighted by remaining prerequisite distance. Confirmation discovers one item, clears the offer, increments cost counts; reroll consumes a saved charge, excludes the former offer and recrafts. Empty offers fall back to idle. Ritual discovery requires recipe-book availability, all prerequisite rituals discovered, and discover requirements. It can be offered before its usage prerequisites are satisfied, because those separately supply discovery-range distance; unmet usage increases activation cost and shows an insufficient-state warning.

Ritual activation enters real wave combat. Ongoing resource drain fills completion slots; enemy death weight also fills slots by spending currently available resources. Full completion requires at least five waves plus fully filled slots. Player death ends the run; a run is classed failed only below five waves, independently of the full-completion predicate.

End grants instant rewards proportional to waves even before the early-failure branch. Failure refunds raw activationCost times one minus the player fail penalty and exits before duration/permanent rewards or completion events. Success installs duration instances, updates highest reached level, raises completion events, and reapplies permanent effects scaled from the highest reach. Permanent means current-run persistent effects, not NG+ retention: RitualSO lacks IPersistentReset and ResetData clears discovery/reach/instances/effects.

Duration instances carry level/power/duration; reload reinitializes and reapplies their player status effects. They expire from played-time increments and remove associated modifiers. Non-echo active instances influence repeated-activation penalties and chain length for later rituals.

Research has separate capacity use and consumed development resources. UIResearchItem disables cost-button payment; Develop/Queue applies researchCost as keyed resource usage, while totalCost fills by resource drain. Insufficient supply lowers drain ratio and progress. Queue selects affordable/legal future levels and continuation starts after level completion. Cancel clears investment and queue; pause retains the investment. Reached levels enable prerequisite links and apply persistent reward blocks.

The actual time-screen reset route requires complete-world-cycle and fetched challenges. Initial challenge fetch is free; later rerolls require positive reroll tokens and consume one. CompleteWorldCycle completes active finish-the-game challenges, refills rerolls, marks world complete, and adds a two-point pending-cycle contribution to starting time advancements. Serialized WorldComplete is raised by the final Restoration ritual and routed through listener11406.

Persistent reset captures each saveable IPersistentReset object only when its IsPersistent() is true, resets it, reloads its captured state and invokes its callback; all other IResetable objects reset. Global seed is salted. Then manager clears completed/fetched flags, retains last persistence value, clears cycle timer, activates pending rewards/new challenges, increments reset count, derives persistent-resource maximum from last persistence, and reloads the scene without ordinary full reset.

Time runes always enter the retain/reload path, but their callback then clears current level, discovered flag and rarity. Mastery level/XP and seen flag survive; mastery consumers are reapplied to player and rune types on initialization. Research persists only when any assigned ResearchType has persistThroughReset. Achievements, challenges and keybindings always return persistent; advancement/number variables depend on asset isPersistent flags; number variables additionally need saveValue to emit saved state.

Challenges retain earned level/state. Specific goals can pass while playing; finish-the-game goals pass when WorldComplete calls CompleteGame. Failure removes current restrictions without advancing level. The actual time-screen Button13504 -> event5070 -> listener17046 -> UITimeScreenManager17107.FetchNewChallenges uses modern ChallengeManager.GenerateNewChallengeList, with compulsory increased-difficulty, weighted types, incompatible/excluded entries and probabilistic preferred entries. The exported legacy modal6292 and PersistentResetManager.FetchNewChallenges contain a deprecated generator path; it is not the reviewed active time-screen route.

Live simulation runs in FixedUpdate with fixedDeltaTime and slow increments every 0.2 seconds. Save load restores state and played time; save-age timestamp is calculated for a variable. No reviewed managed startup/load consumer passes elapsed save age into game simulation, and searches found no game offline/catch-up routine or application-focus/pause hook. This supports no managed catch-up path found, not a whole-installed-game/runtime proof of no offline progress or background behavior.

Automation is explicit and funded: AutoBuy only scans trivial affordable structures after an empty action queue and positive enabled queue capacity, using a five-second timer modified by speed. AutoPurchase instances use engaged resource drains and four times base build time, increase structure quantity then reengage at next cost, and expose removal/refund. This is supported live automation, not evidence of closed-app accrual.

Plot nodes offer another live background path: optional automatic action instances, natural growth only with enough space-use capacity, timed Growing/Resting phases, mastery from active work, and distinct consuming versus exiting/resting actions. Actual late-world species/nodes and numerical growth are serialized content; species catalogue outside the selected chain remains unread.

Actual base discovery options are two; base banked rerolls are zero until rewards improve them. findings.finding: Plots retain separate Idle, Growing and Resting populations. Action usage reserves eligible Idle units unless useAnyStateForCost is true. Plants occupy space across phases. Empty land follows missing plot capacity and enters 40-second serial recovery, so destroying a tree does not immediately make all its land usable. GetTotalUsageCost excludes erraticQuantity; the selected tree assets have hasErraticGrowth=false, so their path does not establish a universal natural-spawn cost.

The selected chain consumes 2 empty units for 1 Oak, 2 Oaks for 1 Force tree, and 2 Force trees for 1 Ironwood. Idle parents stay reserved during paid work. Completion creates the target in Growing and then consumes parents. Occupied space conserves 2, 4 and 8 units. Base capacity 8 fits one Ironwood, while auxiliary moss or a spring needs more space.

CreateWorldPillar opens agromancy. Energize requires purchased Energy Trees; Imbue requires purchased Ironwood Trees; fruit requires purchased Create Fruit Trees; treasure requires completed Treasure Trees research. A link tier and its paid acquisition are distinct. These notes inspect those gates, not the full progression leading to them.

Fuel is a continuous drain rather than an up-front prepaid total. Timer progress is maxed action speed multiplied by ResourceDrain support. The least-supported input slows or stalls work; other drains scale with that bottleneck. Growing and Resting phases advance independently at their own speed.

Base action time differs from maturation and actual time. Parent size, quality and optional space rarity change duration; the speed clamp limits completion to at most once per second. Selected planting and tree conversions run serially, while their resulting Growing timers run in parallel.

Ironwood harvesting drains nominal 50 Skill per second and applies a persistent raw Ironwood rate of 0.002 through HarvestScaling during work. It destroys one tree at completion and has no completion lump output. Fruit and treasure collection instead have no action effects or drain and call a treasure pool only on completion.

Cancel clears all durations and action quantity, then removes fuel drains, effects and usage. If actionEffects is empty, reserved parents become available again, but spent fuel is not refunded. A persistent harvest spends one element-cost batch and rotates or destroys its size because output has already accrued; other reserved units are released. Cancellation is not a universal resource refund.

Force bark has two policies: destroy one Force tree for ongoing Wood and ForceBark during nominal 16-second harvesting, or pay 14 Skill per second for nominal 32-second peeling, which moves one Force tree to Resting for 45 seconds serially and then Growing for 240 seconds in parallel. Fruit and treasure also retain occupancy through recovery and regrowth.

Fruit uses three Oaks and six occupied plot units; treasure uses three Force trees and twelve units. Collection calls EarnPartialTreasure, which retains fractional rewards. Weighted eligible content reaches ConsumableSO.Gain. The Fruit item groups and Core subpools differ; a specific item is not guaranteed.

Non-growing completions trigger node-type consumeEffects, including rating-based Plant Core treasure. Growing tree conversions skip those effects. Refund-rating echoes can add completions without consuming a parent each time. Exact random outcomes remain unverified.

Enrich is a competing sink: it consumes three trees and sends 10 scaled XP to a named Advancement, rather than producing harvest stock or a growing replacement. Its raw duration of 1e-5 seconds still faces the one-second speed clamp. Downstream Advancement progression remains unread.

Unreserved Idle moss supplies a raw Verdant rate of 0.16 and a NaturalResourceType GainRate modifier. A water spring occupies five plots and supplies Water plus PlantNodeType GrowingSpeed and Yield modifiers. Reserving units for work suppresses passive contribution through GetRemainingQuantity. Material, growing speed, yield and occupied capacity remain distinct roles.

Ironwood has an actual alchemy consumer: discovered Extract Ironwood reserves Mechanical capacity and drains nominal 0.012 Ironwood per second. It supplies functional capacity modifiers of 4 Alchemical, 16 Biotic and 8 Occultic units. These are not direct Organic or Occult Essence outputs or input fuel refunds.

ExpertAlchemy level 16 is an Extract Ironwood soft usage condition. Its last core type, Alchemy, defines unmet penalties of double usage, quarter speed, sixteen-fold cost and a 0.97 effect-scaling exponent. Discovery, affordability and full support are separate. The nominal 0.012 drain is not a universal live quote.

Functional capacity effects do not multiply their quoted max modifier by the support ratio. ResourceSO writes that ratio into usageDrainPenalty. Functional max becomes part of nominal capacity, while consumer ResourceDrains propagate the support ratio. Starvation can leave nominal capacity visible while reducing downstream work. Disengaging removes functional modifiers, reservations and drains; spent Ironwood stays spent.

An enabled AutoBuyManager binding exists in level1. Its five-second timer, scaled by speed, runs only with an empty general Actionable list, positive queue size and enabled flag. It scans AllStructures in order, checks availability, level requirements, room and trivial cost, forces single purchases, and queues real construction. Trivial means each true price is less than stock divided by 1000. This manager does not choose or automate agromancy chains.

Assets include debug-like phase quantities, sizes and hasBeenUsed flags. ResetData clears plot quantities, mastery, visibility and modifiers, and clears the action-used flag. These serialized values do not establish a fresh profile or runtime state.

Source anomaly, unverified: EarnTreasure calls Consumable.Gain, then returns a struct without setting success=true. ExecuteEarnTreasure only reports successful results. The acquisition call and its success/logging flag differ. No runtime failure was reproduced or repair assigned.

findings.title: Earned automatic purchasing is a live cheap-action policy
findings.finding: The attribute auto-buyer resets its five-second baseline timer while the action queue is occupied, queue size is zero or its enabled toggle is false. Once idle, it scans available structures in list order, pays one actual next-cost purchase at a time only while cost is trivial and queue allocation remains. Each cost component must be less than one-thousandth of current quantity after true-spend conversion. It does not wait offline or waive material cost.

trace.prerequisites: Actual auto-buyer queue capacity, enabled toggle, empty current action queue and available affordable structures. Authored queue capacity base0 and speed100; first purchased upgrade adds4queue slots. Reset/initialization and modifiers determine live values.
trace.decision: Earn and enable cheap repetitive purchases, manually prioritize larger strategic investments, or turn individual attributes off under the current patch.
trace.cost_time: Five-second baseline / speed factor; each queued purchase calls StructureSO.Purchase, debits its next actual resource cost, and uses action/build timing rather than receiving an immediate grant.
trace.mutation: Paid queued levels progress to quantity; quantity increments feed AttributesDeveloped, drains/rank effects and later passive consumers.
trace.consumer: Actual structure effect and development counters; this can contribute event-based spell recharging, but is not a general spell-autocast routine.
trace.failure_aftermath: Busy/disabled/unearned resets the waiting timer. Nontrivial or insufficient inputs skip that investment. An independent AutoPurchaseInstance is a different drain-backed ongoing mechanism, with its own progress-derived cancellation refund.

findings.larger_original_implication: Earn automation only for known low-risk repeated work with explicit funding and stopping rules. Existing YAIR finite reserves already solve stock-aware repetition, so automatic structure buying itself is not selected as another engine.
